projects.title: FastTracker II Clone
projects.game: FastTracker II for MS-DOS (specific original release not pinned)
projects.platform: FastTracker II for MS-DOS → portable C/SDL2 application for Windows 7 SP1+, macOS 10.11+ (Intel and Apple silicon), and Linux x86-64 packages or source builds
projects.status: The maintainer's download page lists clone v2.26 dated 2026-10-15. It provides Windows and universal macOS builds and links Linux amd64 packages; the maintainer does not support those Linux packages and warns that compiling can depend on the distribution and GCC version. The repository README describes the result as a highly accurate clone, not a full compatibility guarantee.
projects.summary: A portable desktop clone of the classic MS-DOS FastTracker II music tracker. The C/SDL2 application adds newer sample-editing and import features; its author says the XM player is directly ported from the original source with permission and that the code combines original and new code.
projects.strategy: Portable C/SDL2 application that recreates the FastTracker II tracker; selected player code is ported from the original source with permission
projects.source_available: Public GitHub source under BSD-3-Clause; the README attributes some code to the original FastTracker II source and says the port is used with permission
projects.programming_language: C (predominant in GitHub's repository language breakdown), with C++, Objective-C, CMake, and shell build files

projects.title: Webamp
projects.game: Winamp 2 media player (skin-rendering parity documented against Winamp 2.9)
projects.platform: Winamp 2 desktop-player experience → browser app for modern Edge, Firefox, Safari, and Chrome; an Electron desktop wrapper is separately listed by the project
projects.status: The project changelog identifies v2.3.1 as the current Webamp release. The README documents current Edge, Firefox, Safari, and Chrome support and says Internet Explorer is unsupported. The skin documentation states that classic Winamp 2 skins are rendered pixel-for-pixel as in Winamp 2.9; the project does not claim compatibility with Winamp binary plugins or the entire desktop product.
projects.summary: A browser-based Winamp 2 reimplementation built with HTML5 and JavaScript/TypeScript. It recreates the media-player interface and supports classic Winamp 2 skins, with documented pixel-level skin rendering compared with Winamp 2.9.
projects.strategy: Reimplement Winamp 2's player interface and behavior for modern web browsers, including a custom renderer for classic Winamp 2 skins
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source; the README notes that the Winamp name, interface, and sample audio may belong to Nullsoft
projects.programming_language: TypeScript (predominant in the GitHub language breakdown), plus JavaScript and web/build languages

projects.title: JS Paint
projects.game: Classic Microsoft Paint interface and behavior, especially the Windows 95/98/XP-era application
projects.platform: Classic MS Paint-style editor → browser application, including mobile-friendly touch interaction, plus an Electron desktop application for Windows, macOS, and Linux
projects.status: The maintainer describes JS Paint as a pixel-perfect remake of classic MS Paint and says it recreates its tools and menus to a high degree of fidelity. The README says some tools remain incomplete; full clipboard support in the web app requires a browser with the Async Clipboard API for images (the README's Chrome 76+ note is historical). The Electron build is cross-platform, but its README warns that Electron is out of date and automatic updates are not implemented. The repository's latest push checked on 2026-10-15 was 2026-07-19.
projects.summary: An open-source browser and Electron remake of classic Microsoft Paint, aimed at the Windows 95/98/XP-era interface and behavior. It adds modern features such as more undo steps, additional image formats, themes, accessibility options, and touch interaction; it is an application reimplementation rather than a binary-compatible Paint runtime.
projects.strategy: Recreate classic MS Paint's user interface and editing behavior as a web application, with an Electron desktop build
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source repository; maintainer links Electron releases from the README
projects.programming_language: JavaScript (predominant in GitHub's language breakdown), with CSS, HTML, and small TypeScript and shell components
projects.subtype: Raster image editor / classic desktop application remake
